title: Explicit Audit Archive And Prefix Retention
summary: P3E7 adds bounded read-only management audit export, administrator-declared archive preservation, transactional prefix retirement and explicit stale-cursor errors. Archive integrity is checked; external durability and disaster-recovery completeness are not inferred.
successor: P3E8 dev.16 adds the deployment/request identity pin and offline recovery contract in docs/machine/shin-server-recovery-v1.json. Old Server-identity audit retention plans cannot replay after recovery; a new plan must be inspected. Existing archive/plan/receipt formats are unchanged. Recorded P3E7 versions and verification remain historical evidence.

export.authorization: Administrator only. Cross-project management metadata must not be exposed through the project-reader audit API. The Server does not accept a destination path or write an archive file.
export.schema: shin.audit-export.v1 returns archive, plan, read_only=true and external_archive_verified=false. Archive schema shin.audit-archive.v1 contains server_id, retired_through, through_id, exact events and previous_retention_receipt plus explicit service-observed/non-source authority flags.
export.bounds: 1..1000 events, default 256. Compact archive is at most 1MiB; larger requests fail audit-export-budget and must be retried explicitly with fewer events. No full-log scan or automatic multi-page drain. IDs can contain rollback gaps: event_count is an actual row count, not subtraction of cursor values.
export.digest: SHA256 over archive.dump(): nlohmann compact sorted-key JSON, UTF-8, no indentation or trailing newline. Plan binds exact archive bytes/hash, Server identity, retired floor, through_id, event_count and previous receipt hash. plan_id is SHA256 of the same compact serialization of the plan without plan_id. Hashes are integrity identifiers, not signatures or proof of external storage.
export.consistency: Acquire the existing audit-writers transaction advisory lock in shared mode before reading history and rows. All public audit writers acquire its exclusive mode before allocating IDs, preserving commit-order cursor semantics. Export runs no DML and writes no export receipt or management event. Repeated exports of the same prefix are identical. Later appended events do not invalidate that fixed prefix.

retention.request: Exact {plan:<inspected plan>,archive_saved:true}. Administrator must first preserve and independently verify the exported archive in a reviewed external destination. archive_saved is a caller declaration, not an independent Server durability check. The API never runs or schedules the next step itself.
retention.transaction: Exclusive audit-writers fence; compare the current exact prefix and archive digest; delete only its bounded rows; advance retired_through and lifetime retired_events; persist the latest plan/receipt together. Failed state update or commit rolls back deletion. No stream, workspace, preparation, activation, source or observer cursor is changed.
retention.receipt: shin.audit-retention-receipt.v1 binds plan_id, Server, previous/new floors, deleted_events, archive hash/bytes, previous_receipt_sha256, administrator identity and recorded_at. archive_saved_declared=true, external_archive_verified=false and shared_publication_mutated=false remain explicit. recorded_at is transaction observation time, not an independently measured commit timestamp.
retention.replay: Only the exact latest plan can replay its persisted receipt, including after restart. Older plans conflict after another prune; this is not an unbounded operation ledger. Concurrent exact retries commit one deletion. Empty plans fail audit-retention-empty. The latest retention receipt is included in the next archive, and hashes link receipts without recursively growing the singleton.
retention.locking: Retention holds only the global audit fence while accessing audit_events/audit_history and reading immutable Server identity. It must never acquire stream/workspace/preparation locks after this fence, because their normal writers acquire it last. Existing statement/lock deadlines remain enforced.
retention.ledger: Migration 009 adds a singleton audit_history with bounded latest plan/receipt metadata. It preserves every existing event and receipt and initializes no historical deletion. Prior migration checksums are unchanged. Runtime gets DELETE on audit_events and SELECT/UPDATE on audit_history, but no public arbitrary SQL/delete endpoint. Retention is recorded in this separate singleton, not as a fabricated project-scoped event.

reading.status: GET /api/v1/audit/history is administrator-only, read-only and returns Server identity, retired_through, retired_events and last_retention_receipt. It does not claim external archive availability or complete lifetime history.
reading.cursor: GET /api/v1/audit keeps its existing project/Observer-owner filtering. An authorized reader cursor below retired_through fails HTTP 410 audit-history-retired rather than silently jumping over missing history. The error exposes no global floor or retired event count. An administrator can supply a reviewed current floor; after equal to the floor explicitly reads retained history only. Principals with no project access still receive the existing empty result without inspecting global history.

limits: No automatic age policy, background deletion, export daemon or client archive manager is installed.
An administrator can falsely declare archive_saved. Durable external storage, restore rehearsal, retention/legal policy and custody are operator responsibilities, not validated evidence.
Exported management metadata is sensitive operational data; use a private external archive and never commit it into a consumer repository or publish it as KB authority.
The current Server ID is not a backup/PITR epoch. Restoring an older database can lose floors and receipts. Backup/restore lineage and inactive stream retirement remain separate work.
This bounds each retention operation and singleton metadata, not total PostgreSQL disk, WAL or audit growth between explicit operations. PostgreSQL vacuum and database backup policies are separate.
No Observer delivery protocol, local state, Core index format, global skill or stable consumer route changes.
